meta.chapterLabel: Lesson 15: Talking about Preferences: I Like Japanese Anime

items.note: な-adjective; often written すき(な) (suki(na)) since な (na) attaches before a noun, e.g. すきな アニメ (sukina anime), 'favorite anime'. Conjugates: すきです (sukidesu) 'like', すきじゃありません (sukija arimasen) 'don't like', すきでした (sukideshita) 'liked', すきじゃありませんでした (sukija arimasendeshita) 'didn't like'.
items.reviewNote: (な) stripped from the source headword すき(な) — a type marker, not part of the spoken word. Conjugation forms are drawn from the EXERCISES I present/past aff./neg. reference chart (image) rather than given four separate cards.

items.note: The dictionary form of かきます (kakimasu) — see GRAMMAR 2 on forming dictionary forms.
items.hint: wants the dictionary (plain) form, not the ます form

items.note: The ます-form (masu-form, used in polite speech) of かく (kaku), which this lesson introduces as the word's dictionary form.
items.hint: wants the ます (polite) form, not the dictionary form

items.english: (nominalizer — turns a verb into a noun-like phrase, similar to '-ing')
items.note: Added after a verb's dictionary form so the action can take が (ga), as in サッカーを みるのが すきです (sakkā o miru no ga sukidesu), 'likes watching soccer' (KS3).
items.reviewNote: Possibly already taught — already introduced in Lesson 1: Meeting: Nice to Meet You (matched on target)

items.note: な-adjective; often written じょうず(な) (jouzu(na)). Conjugates: じょうずです (jouzudesu) 'be good at', じょうずじゃありません (jouzu ja arimasen) 'not good at', じょうずでした (jouzudeshita) 'was good at', じょうずじゃありませんでした (jouzu ja arimasendeshita) 'wasn't good at'. Almost never used to describe yourself or your own family — it sounds like boasting.
items.reviewNote: Conjugation forms and the self-description caveat come from GRAMMAR 1's NOTE and the EXERCISES I reference chart (image).

items.english: What kind of anime do you like?
items.target: どんなアニメがすきですか
items.pronunciation: donna anime ga suki desu ka
items.note: どんな (donna, 'what kind of') was already met in Lesson 10 (どんなところですか, 'what kind of place'); here it combines with the new が すきですか pattern to ask what someone likes within a category.
items.reviewNote: Quoted verbatim in NOTES 1 as the illustration of どんな; also the dialogue's opening question to Paul.

items.note: Short for わたしも ロボットの アニメが すきです (watashi mo robotto no anime ga sukidesu), 'I like mecha anime too'. Can express agreement whether the previous statement was affirmative or negative.

items.note: Dictionary form of します (shimasu) — one of only two Irregular verbs, along with くる (kuru). Combines with many nouns to form compound verbs, e.g. べんきょうします (benkyō shimasu), 'study'.

items.note: A Regular 2 verb — already in its dictionary form (Regular 2 verbs form the dictionary form by changing ます (masu) to る (ru)).
Dictionary form of ききます (kikimasu). ききます already covered 'ask' (Lesson 9) besides 'listen, hear' (Lesson 8); きく carries both senses too — context tells them apart.

items.english: Mr. Kato doesn't like coffee. He's not good at tennis.
items.target: かとうさんはコーヒーがすきじゃありません。テニスがじょうずじゃありません
items.pronunciation: katō san wa kōhī ga suki ja ari mase n. tenisu ga jōzu ja ari mase n
items.reviewNote: e.g. line from EXERCISES II.B — the chapter's only complete sentence demonstrating the negative forms すきじゃありません / じょうずじゃありません.

items.english: What kind of sports do you like?
items.target: どんなスポーツがすきですか
items.pronunciation: donna supōtsu ga suki desu ka
items.reviewNote: e.g. line from EXERCISES III — a second どんな example with different vocabulary from NOTES 1's, per the 'two examples beat one' guidance.

items.note: イタリア (itaria, 'Italy') + りょうり (ryouri, 'cuisine') = イタリアりょうり (itaria ryouri), 'Italian cuisine'.
The base word decomposed from イタリアりょうり (itaria ryouri), 'Italian cuisine', above.

items.english: Do you like listening to music, Green-san?
items.target: グリーンさんはおんがくをきくのがすきですか
items.pronunciation: gurīn san wa on gaku o kiku no ga suki desu ka
items.reviewNote: e.g. line from EXERCISES VII — a second example of the の nominalizer pattern (verb dictionary form + の + が すきです), for variety alongside KS3.

Not formally glossed in this chapter's VOCABULARY tables; appears in EXERCISES III's blank cue and EXERCISES VII's e.g. sentence. Gloss supplied from general knowledge. | Possibly already taught — already introduced in Lesson 8: Doing Things (1): I’m Going to Eat Tempura (matched on english)

items.english: I like soccer. But I'm not good at it.
items.target: サッカーがすきです。でも、じょうずじゃありません
items.pronunciation: sakkā ga suki desu. demo, jōzu ja ari mase n
items.reviewNote: From SPEAKING PRACTICE 1 (Raja's line) — the chapter's only sentence using でも (but), extracted under the dialogue-line exception since でも's own vocabulary entry needs a worked example.

items.target: グリーンさんははしるのがすきです
items.pronunciation: Gurīn-san wa hashiru no ga suki desu
items.note: はしる is the dictionary form of はしります — の turns the verb into a noun-like phrase so it can take が.
